subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If the point (1, 2, 3) is changed to the point (2, 3, 1) through translation of axes, find the new origin.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 5 THREE DIMENSIONAL COORDINATES, Very Short Answer question 11, book p.177. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. FILING NOTE: translation of axes is a change-of-axes topic rather than a three-dimensional-coordinates one, but the book prints this question inside chapter 5 THREE DIMENSIONAL COORDINATES, and we file it in unit 5 as the book does so that a student who works through the printed chapter finds every question of it here. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what a translation of axes does to a point's coordinates, and which way round the subtraction goes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the translation rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. In a translation the axes keep their directions and only the origin moves, so each new coordinate is the old one minus the matching coordinate of the new origin.
steps.memory_tip: New coordinate = old coordinate − new origin, one coordinate at a time.
lines: Let the new origin be O' = (h, k, l).
In a translation of axes the directions of
the axes do not change, so a point (x, y, z)
gets new coordinates (X, Y, Z) where
X = x − h,  Y = y − k,  Z = z − l

recall.must_convey: That under a translation of axes the new coordinates are the old coordinates minus the new origin, written as X = x − h, Y = y − k, Z = z − l.
accept: the new coordinates are the old ones minus the new origin
X equals x minus h, Y equals y minus k, Z equals z minus l
only the origin moves, the axis directions stay the same
translation lo axes direction marchadu, origin matrame move avuthundi
write the translation rule with the given point and its new coordinates
reject: the new origin is minus one, minus one, two

steps.why: The rule has to be written the right way round before any numbers go in. The axes do not turn, so each coordinate is handled on its own and the shift is a plain subtraction.
common_mistakes: Writing X = x + h, which moves the origin the wrong way.
Treating the change as a rotation, where the axis directions would also change.

steps.label: Solve for the new origin
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three separate one-line equations. Substitute the answer back into the rule to make sure the shift is the right way round.
steps.memory_tip: New origin = old point − new point: (1, 2, 3) − (2, 3, 1) = (−1, −1, 2).

recall.must_convey: That solving the three equations gives the new origin (−1, −1, 2), and that substituting it back returns (2, 3, 1).
accept: h is minus one, k is minus one and l is two
the new origin is the old point minus the new point
moodu equations separate ga solve chesi new origin ravali
put it back and check the point becomes two three one
reject: the new coordinates are the old ones minus the new origin

steps.why: The subtraction is easy to reverse by accident, so the check matters: transforming (1, 2, 3) forward through the answer must give back (2, 3, 1) exactly.
common_mistakes: Giving (1, 1, −2), which is the new point minus the old point.
Stopping at the three equations without solving for h, k and l.
